er_v06_c06_b001_02: After last time, I figured things out. Life goes on. Besides, I'm almost used to the stench.
er_v06_c06_b001_03: First priority: survival. So I went scavenging at the dump.
er_v06_c06_b001_04: My roommate gave me a crash course in scavenging. I have to admit, there's a real community spirit down here.
er_v06_c06_b001_05: Anyway, come look at what I found! ...Don't laugh.
er_v06_c06_b002_01: I think this one's usable. That one's old, but the inside is fine.
er_v06_c06_b002_03: You don't have to say every piece is good just to make me feel better.
er_v06_c06_b002_04: Then this one gets a lower price. It's broken here.
er_v06_c06_b002_05: ...So that wasn't dirt? I spent ages wiping it.
er_v06_c06_b002_07: That one was just to make me feel better.
er_v06_c06_b003_01: Good. You take the goods, I take the credits.
er_v06_c06_b003_02: This is much better than standing here waiting for you to pity me.
er_v06_c06_b004_03: Then you'll have to tell me what it's normally worth. I have to learn.
er_v06_c06_b005_01: Is that price because the goods aren't worth much, or because you think I can only sell to you?
er_v06_c06_b006_01: It's fine. I'll remember what you don't buy and bring something else next time.
er_v06_c06_b007_01: I've been thinking about what to do next.
er_v06_c06_b007_02: I'm sure someone in the upper district set up my mother. I can't go up there and ask around, but a private investigator can.
er_v06_c06_b007_03: A reliable one costs eight hundred credits.
er_v06_c06_b007_05: I know. So I'll keep scavenging and sell what I find to you.
er_v06_c06_b007_06: Give me a fair price, all right? Every credit gets me closer.
er_v06_c06_b007_07: I've asked other buyers too, and I took some short work cleaning grow tanks. I can't rely on your shop alone.
er_v06_c06_b007_08: Write down what you earned today.
er_v06_c06_b007_09: Already did. Don't think you're the only one on this station who can keep accounts.
er_v06_c07_b001_01: Hey, me again. Don't look at the goods first today.
er_v06_c07_b001_02: How am I supposed to buy without looking?
er_v06_c07_b001_03: I'll quote first. Then you tell me what I got wrong.
er_v06_c07_b001_05: This casing is dented, but the inside's fine, so normal price. This one looks new, but the connector's rusted, so lower it. This one... I'm not sure.
er_v06_c07_b001_06: Two right, one unsure. Last time's lesson wasn't wasted.
er_v06_c07_b001_07: You didn't charge tuition. It doesn't count as a lesson.
er_v06_c07_b001_08: Then I'll start charging next time.
er_v06_c07_b001_09: You can't charge for lessons already given!
er_v06_c07_b002_01: At the dump today, someone tried to trade me a bag of broken parts for my stuff. Said I clearly didn't know the market.
er_v06_c07_b002_03: Of course not! I told him to take it to the pawnshop and let the owner decide what it's worth.
er_v06_c07_b003_01: The moment he heard it was your shop, he turned around and left faster than I did.
er_v06_c07_b003_02: I didn't expect your shop's name to carry more weight than my family name down here.
er_v06_c07_b003_03: It only works when I'm buying scrap.
er_v06_c07_b003_04: Still better than my name. My name can't even buy scrap now.
er_v06_c07_b004_01: He said he'd never heard of any pawnshop, muttered something, and left.
er_v06_c07_b004_02: At least I didn't get fooled. That's the important part.
er_v06_c07_b005_01: Add today's sale, and we're one step closer to eight hundred.
er_v06_c07_b005_02: Did you set aside food money?
er_v06_c07_b005_03: I did. Nutrifruit doesn't taste like punishment every meal now.
er_v06_c07_b006_01: You know, I used to think helping someone meant throwing a fortune at them.
er_v06_c07_b006_02: Now I know that someone honestly buying what I scavenged at a fair price is enough to keep me going.
er_v06_c07_b007_01: Don't tell me again that this is just what the lower levels pay. I've asked other buyers.
er_v06_c07_b007_02: Things are worth what they're worth. They don't become worth less because I'm in a hurry.
er_v06_c08_b001_01: Wait, don't put this with the rest.
er_v06_c08_b001_04: You still need money for the investigator.
er_v06_c08_b001_05: I know. This doesn't come out of that.
er_v06_c08_b001_06: Last time you were buying, you looked at this kind of material a little longer. I found some, so I kept it.
er_v06_c08_b001_08: I don't just stand here waiting to count your money.
er_v06_c08_b001_09: Don't get the wrong idea. I just have good eyes.
er_v06_c08_b002_02: Good. When you use it, don't tell people you just picked it up somewhere.
er_v06_c08_b003_01: This is something I wanted to give you. If you insist on paying, fine.
er_v06_c08_b003_02: But you should know, this time I'm not asking you for help.
er_v06_c08_b004_02: Fine. Next time I'll pick something you can't find an excuse to refuse.
er_v06_c08_b005_01: My roommate asked how I knew you'd be open today.
er_v06_c08_b005_03: I said anyone running a proper business opens on time.
er_v06_c08_b005_05: She asked why I don't go to another shop.
er_v06_c08_b005_07: Then I told her to mind her own radio and stop playing it at midnight.
er_v06_c08_b005_08: What are you laughing at? She really is loud!
er_v06_c08_b006_01: I'll slowly pay back what you've done for me.
er_v06_c08_b006_02: You don't have to say that every time you come.
er_v06_c08_b006_03: Then this is the last time I'll say it. From now on, watch what I do.
er_v06_c09_b001_01: So this is the shop Eleanor never stops talking about?
er_v06_c09_b001_03: I know. I picked a time when she wouldn't be.
er_v06_c09_b001_05: Selling. *sets a bracelet on the counter* I'll name the price. You decide what to pay.
er_v06_c09_b001_06: She says you have a sharp eye. I'd like to see how sharp.
er_v06_c09_b002_01: You priced it too low. Upper-district handmade work. The clasp was replaced, but it doesn't hurt the value.
er_v06_c09_b002_02: ...You can tell the clasp was replaced?
er_v06_c09_b002_03: The new clasp is brighter than the band.
er_v06_c09_b003_02: She said you never take advantage of people. I suppose it depends on whose advantage it is.
er_v06_c09_b004_01: You won't buy it? Fine. At least you didn't pretend to know.
er_v06_c09_b005_01: She used to buy things based only on whether she liked the look. She never asked the price.
er_v06_c09_b005_02: Now she asks more questions than anyone.
er_v06_c09_b005_03: She told me. She said when you buy goods, you put the fault on the item, not the person.
er_v06_c09_b005_05: Her exact words were much ruder. I picked the part I could repeat.
er_v06_c09_b005_06: I can find her a job up there. A place to live too.
er_v06_c09_b005_08: I did. She has one condition: stop bringing up her mother's case in public. She won't agree.
er_v06_c09_b005_09: Then she's already given you her answer.
er_v06_c09_b005_10: She keeps saying 'there are people down here too.' I thought she was just being stubborn.
er_v06_c09_b005_11: ...What exactly have you people done to her?
er_v06_c09_b006_01: If she asks, tell her I came to sell something.
er_v06_c09_b006_02: I'll tell her everything you said.
er_v06_c09_b006_03: ...Suit yourself. Just don't make me sound better than I was.
er_v06_c10_b001_02: She did. Sold a bracelet, and mentioned she could find you a job up there.
er_v06_c10_b001_05: I turned her down. Not because the job was bad.
er_v06_c10_b001_06: I can't live in a house someone else gives me, learn to keep my mouth shut, and pretend my mother doesn't exist.
er_v06_c10_b001_10: She also asked whether you were only interested because I used to have money, waiting for the day I recover so you can cash in.
er_v06_c10_b002_01: I said that when everyone else changed their expression the moment they heard my name, you were still looking down at the goods.
er_v06_c10_b002_02: On my poorest days, you didn't suddenly get better at arithmetic.
er_v06_c10_b003_01: I said you've done things that made me furious. But you came back and made them right.
er_v06_c10_b003_02: I know what happened better than she does. She doesn't get to decide for me.
er_v06_c10_b004_01: I said I'd judge for myself. ...If you really are waiting for me to recover before you start offering fair prices, you'd better stop waiting.
er_v06_c10_b005_01: You don't have to vouch for my shop.
er_v06_c10_b005_02: Who's vouching for you? I have confidence in my own judgement.
er_v06_c10_b005_03: She said I never used to admit I'd misjudged someone.
er_v06_c10_b005_05: Now I do. For example, I used to think everyone down here was the same.
er_v06_c10_b005_06: Don't get smug. I'm not right about people every time either.
er_v06_c10_b006_01: By the way. Did she also praise your eye for goods?
er_v06_c10_b006_03: She praises everyone like that. Don't take it seriously.
er_v06_c10_b006_04: ...And don't talk to her too long. That mouth of hers could talk anyone in circles.
er_v06_c10_b006_05: I've sold out for today. Can I stay here a little longer?
er_v06_c10_b006_06: Only when there are no customers.
er_v06_c10_b006_07: Fine. It's not as if I'm here to keep you from making money.
